title: The Price of You
gist: Lindsay Owens warns that firms increasingly set individualized online prices using personal data such as purchase history, location, demographics, behavior and biometrics, and that AI chatbots threaten to turbocharge this surveillance pricing, widening the gap between privacy expectations and reality.

insights.claim: As more people shop online, firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior and biometric data.
insights.speaker: LINDSAY OWENS
insights.so_what: Personalized pricing is a growing retail margin lever and a growing regulatory and reputational risk for e-commerce and data-driven retailers.
insights.quote: firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data, including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior, and biometric data

insights.claim: AI threatens to turbocharge surveillance pricing, further widening the gap between consumers' privacy expectations and reality.
insights.speaker: LINDSAY OWENS
insights.so_what: Signals likely regulatory and political backlash targeting AI-enabled pricing and data sharing, a risk for AI commerce business models.
insights.quote: AI threatens to turbocharge such surveillance pricing

insights.claim: In a hypothetical scenario, an AI chatbot recommending a thermometer could share a user's prior queries about a sick child's symptoms with the recommended retailer, which then raises the price knowing the parent is worried.
insights.speaker: LINDSAY OWENS
insights.so_what: Highlights the conflict of interest when chatbots monetize via commerce links and data sharing, a flashpoint for consumer-protection scrutiny of AI assistants.
insights.quote: Armed with the knowledge that you are a parent worried about a child’s spiking fever, the retailer hikes the price.
insights.locator: WASHINGTON, DC—You ask an AI chatbot

themes.theme: Privacy gap and undisclosed data sharing

insights.claim: The danger of chatbot-mediated shopping is that data sharing with retailers can be undisclosed: the user sees a confident, friendly recommendation without being told their sensitive queries were passed on.
insights.speaker: LINDSAY OWENS
insights.so_what: Opacity of AI recommendation pipelines strengthens the case for disclosure mandates on AI agents in commerce.
insights.quote: What the chatbot neglects to mention is that it shared your previous queries
insights.locator: WASHINGTON, DC—You ask an AI chatbot
